topics.label: Introduction and cancer hallmarks overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture topic, outlines learning objectives regarding cancer hallmarks, and frames the multi-step progression model.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and signaling cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive autonomous proliferation and escape from growth inhibition.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells experience a differentiation block that arrests maturation and maintains proliferative states in hematopoietic and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the molecular mechanisms and regulatory alterations that enable cancer cells to resist apoptotic cell death via the p53 and Bcl-2 pathways.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells achieve replicative immortality by overcoming telomere shortening and bypassing p53-mediated senescence.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism and metabolic reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine metabolic alterations in cancer cells, including the Warburg effect, metabolic pathway rewiring, and the epigenetic impact of oncometabolites.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the physiological necessity of tumor vascularization, its onset during neoplastic progression, and the balance of signals controlling vessel formation.

topics.label: Invasion, dissemination, and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the multi-step cascade of tumor metastasis, clinical methods for detecting disseminated cells, and genomic factors supporting colonization.

topics.label: Conclusion and lecture wrap-up
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer provides concluding remarks on the synthesis of cancer hallmarks, suggests further reading, and closes the session.
